chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says at the end of the prostration of the voluntary prayer after Maghrib on the night of Friday, and if he says it every night it is better: 'O God, I ask You by Your Noble Face and Your Great Name that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and that You forgive me my great sin' seven times, he departs having been forgiven.

He said: And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When it is the evening of Thursday and the night of Friday, angels descend from the sky with them golden pens and silver tablets; they do not write except the prayer upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on the evening of Thursday, the night of Friday, and the day of Friday until the sun sets. Travel and running errands on Friday are disliked due to the prayer, but after the prayer it is permissible and one may be blessed by it.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and etiquette for Friday night in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the unique spiritual status of Friday night (Laylat al-Jumu'ah) as a time when angels record blessings upon the Prophet using golden pens, linking this celestial activity to the prohibition of travel and worldly errands until sunset. The specific dhikr of seeking forgiveness through the Prophet's name and that of his Ahl al-Bayt underscores the Shia emphasis on intercession (Tawassul) and the transformative power of voluntary prayers (Salat al-Nafil) in securing divine mercy.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-95 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ayoob ibn Nooh, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

Whoever says the following supplications at the end of the prostration of the recommendable (Nafila) prayer after the eve of Friday night, ‘O my Lord! I beseech you by your Noble Face and Grand Name that you send blessingsupon Muhammad and his household and that you forgive my major sins’ for seven times would be forgiven by God just when he lifts his head off from the position of prostration.’”

Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) also said, “Angels who carry golden pens and silver tablets descend to the Earth on Thursday nights and Fridays. They only record the reward of sending blessings upon Muhammad and his household on Thursday nights and Fridays. It is not recommendable to go after your needs on Fridays before the Friday prayer, but it is fine to do so afterwards.”
